title: Homo neanderthalensis (Neanderthals)
note: Parent of the extinction record. Smithsonian Human Origins gives c. 400,000–40,000 years ago, range Europe and southwestern to central Asia; first/last appearance, range over time, Feldhofer 1856 and King's 1864 naming.

title: Denisovans
note: Asian archaic population; Prüfer et al. 2014 (PMC4031459): Denisova Cave sublayer 11.2 c. 50,300 years ago, ≥0.5% Neanderthal DNA, Denisovan ancestry ~25x higher in Papuans and Australians than in mainland Asians. Strong Oceania/Asia coverage value; check later finds outside the Altai.

title: Shanidar Cave Neanderthal burials, Iraqi Kurdistan
note: Western Asian Neanderthal site, under-recorded region; burial-practice debate (the Smithsonian page mentions graves marked with offerings such as flowers). Dates not yet verified; year is a placeholder to be sourced.

title: Uluzzian technocomplex, earliest dated modern human industry in Europe
note: Italy and Greece; early dates of about 45,000 years and shell beads (Oxford/Tübingen release 2014; Douka 2011 work). Attribution to modern humans debated.

title: Gorham's Cave Complex, Gibraltar
note: UNESCO WHC 1500 (2016), N36 7 21.61 W5 20 31.42, four caves, ~120,000 years of Neanderthal and early modern human occupation, engravings older than 39,000 years. Place record needs a model if importance ≥ 3.

title: Phlegraean Fields caldera eruption, c. 39,850 years ago
note: Zilhão et al. 2017 (PMC5696381) give 39,850 years ago and link it to the Ebro barrier; check its proposed role in Neanderthal decline.
